newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Prisoner dies in Colombian jail bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: Prisoner dies in Colombian jail bomb blast.

text.p: A prisoner in Bogota's high-security jail was killed when a bomb he was handling exploded, a prison spokesman said on Sunday.
The blast occurred late on Saturday in a cell close to the wing of the La Picota jail where the Cali drug cartel bosses, the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers, are imprisoned.
The man who died was William Infante, 33, a contract killer serving a 24-year term for the murder of the leader of the left- wing Patriotic Union (UP) party in 1987, the spokesman said.
Another man, Luis Rodriguez Cuadrado, convicted of an assassination attempt on one of President Ernesto Samper's attorneys, was seriously injured in the explosion.

"There was an incident in which a prisoner was handling explosives. We do not yet know exactly what type of explosive it was. The prisoner died in the blast," the spokesman said. He said it was not yet clear how Infante had obtained the explosives.

The spokesman said investigators had ruled out the idea that Infante may have died in a bungled escape bid and said there was no suggestion that the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers, the jail's star convicts, were in any way involved.

According to Colombia's leading El Tiempo newspaper, Infante murdered UP leader Jaime Pardo Leal on the orders of the late drug trafficker Gonzalo Rodriguez Gacha, a henchman of cocaine kingpin Pablo Escobar, the late head of the Medellin cartel.
